note: Laburnum: an ornamental tree with hanging clusters of yellow flowers, whose seeds are poisonous.
Importunate: persistently pressing, troublesome. Desperation presses her to a rash act.
Cerements: the cloth wrappings in which a corpse is buried, a shroud.
Scrutiny: close, careful examination. The poem asks the reader not to probe her private story.
Mutiny: open rebellion against authority. Here it is her rebellion against life, and against the rules of her society.
Eve, the first woman in the Book of Genesis. Hood reminds readers that the fallen girl shares in the common human family, which sinned in Adam and Eve.
source: The Bible (King James Version), Genesis 3, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10

note: Dissolute: lacking moral restraint, given to vice. Hood speaks to the men whose conduct helped destroy her.

anchor: Lave in it, drink of it
note: Lave: to wash or bathe. The poet challenges the reader to enter the same cold river.
Contumely: insolent, humiliating treatment, scornful abuse by others.
